finding: BACK signals with edge_pct >= 12 and decimal_odds >= 3.0 have gone 0-for-18 with -£75.81 P&L since inception (broken down: 3.0-5.0 odds n=6 0% WR -£27.04; 5-10 odds n=4 0% WR -£24.24; 10+ odds n=8 0% WR -£24.53). Meanwhile 12+pp backs in the odds 2.0-3.0 sweet spot are the ONLY profitable slice of the 12+pp back band (n=13, 69.2% WR, +£62.31). The existing MOD-246 ceiling (max_back_edge_pct=15.0) doesn't catch this — every one of the 18 losers had edge_pp in [12.0, 15.0). Also confirmed the leak is still live post-fix: 8 of the 41 total 12+pp backs occurred after MOD-296's phantom-edge fix (2026-07-02), and all 8 lost — including one on 2026-08-16 (Min Woo Lee vs J.J. Spaun, 12.1pp, -£2.00).
root_cause: Longshot-back mis-calibration. The keyword model + Wang transform combine to produce inflated model_prob on low-market-prob runners (favourite-fade engine, MOD-280): when a runner is priced at 15-30% implied, even modest keyword boosts push model_prob well above market, generating a 12+pp 'edge' that has no real research substrate. The residual Wang back-lean (MOD-326, ~0.6-7.3pp per signal) and periodic missing-runners phantom-edge (MOD-296 fixed the consequence but researcher.py still doesn't populate number_of_runners at source) contribute additional artificial back-side inflation. At odds 2.0-3.0 the model's edge is small enough relative to the true distribution that it still adds value; at odds >= 3.0 the compounded artifact swamps signal and results collapse to zero.
proposed_change: In analyze_research.py, immediately after the MOD-246 max_back_edge_pct check (around line 2224, before the MOD-256 min-odds check at line 2231), add a new suppression: if recommendation == 'back' and edge_pp >= 12.0 and _sig_odds is not None and _sig_odds >= 3.0, log 'MOD-XXX: suppressed longshot BACK ... edge Xpp @ odds Y >= 3.0 longshot-inflation guard' and `continue`. Read both thresholds from config with defaults 12.0 and 3.0 (e.g. thresholds.longshot_back_edge_floor_pct=12.0, thresholds.longshot_back_odds_floor=3.0) so the operator can tune without a code edit. Do NOT touch the existing MOD-246 ceiling — keep max_back_edge_pct=15.0 in place for the odds<3.0 population. This is a strict superset of the existing gate for the specific losing slice, leaves the 2-3 odds sweet spot intact, and is one-line-revertible.
expected_impact: Removes the -£75.81 historical drag from 18 trades that all lost. Applied forward: eliminates ~1-3 losing paper signals per month at recent rates (8 losers in the 6 weeks post-MOD-296 = ~1.3/week). Estimated overall win-rate lift +1-2pp (small — the change removes losers but the base was already lay-only-focused, so back reduction has muted top-line effect). Estimated P&L lift ~£5-15/month at current flat £2 stake, extrapolating from the 8-in-6-weeks recent leak. Impact magnitude is derived from data; the projection forward assumes the leak rate holds, which is a guess.
test_condition: After deployment: track count of 'longshot-inflation guard' suppression log lines in data/logs/. Expect 1-3/week initially. Verdict on P&L requires 20+ additional resolved trades in either the >=12pp/>=3.0-odds band (should now be zero) or observation that no new 12+pp backs at odds>=3.0 appear in paper_tracker.json for 30+ days. Complementary check: 12+pp backs at odds 2.0-3.0 should continue to produce signals and maintain > 50% WR — if that band's flow drops materially, the gate is over-firing and should be re-scoped.

evidence.source: data/paper_tracker.json aggregated by edge_pct and decimal_odds

2026-08-16, Min Woo Lee vs J.J. Spaun (golf Match Bet), edge 12.1pp, LOSS -£2.00 — leak is active

alternative_findings: Back-side is losing overall (-£77.00 across 475 trades, ROI -8.1%) while lays are the only profitable side (+£20.72 across 110 trades) — consistent with MOD-280's lay-only reframe. Suggests the standard_track_backs re-enable that produced most of the 475 backs (probably via probe promotion) may need re-evaluation, but that's a broader strategy question, not a targeted code fix.

Lays at 7-9pp show 17.5% WR / -£6.74 (n=40) vs 34.0% WR / +£2.09 (n=47) at 12+pp — a 5pp lay floor lift (from 7 to 10) is defensible but weaker signal than the back finding above (smaller magnitude, smaller sample).
5 recent Match Odds lays at 11.4-15.7pp all lost 0/5 (£-2.44 combined) — very small sample; watch but don't act.

Top boost words 'won' (2995), 'injury' (2044), 'strong' (1000) dominate the boost frequency table — worth an audit of whether generic terms like 'won'/'strong' are triggering on unrelated contexts (e.g. 'won last week' vs 'won the tournament last year'), but not surfaceable as a single testable change without a keyword-level correlation study.
caveats: Sample of 18 for the primary slice is modest, but 0/18 is p < 0.001 under a null 30% WR — the direction is not sample noise. The odds-tiered pattern (2-3 profitable, >=3 catastrophic) rests on n=13 vs n=18 respectively; the profitable 2-3 slice could still regress. The 41 total 12+pp backs accumulated over the full paper history — recent rate is only 8 in 6 weeks, so verifying the fix worked will take 4-6 weeks of clean data. Independent confirmation would come from re-checking edge_traces.json to see whether the 18 losing signals share a specific keyword-boost pattern; not done here.
